children.value: This chapter describes how the associations between the questionnaire scores and the parameters of the latent-state model are estimated (RQ3). The models follow the conventions of the RQ2 questionnaire models: the same five focal questionnaires, the same coding of the instruction condition, the same focal-term logic and the same correction for multiple testing. The six parameters of the adopted model (

): precision weighting, noise reactivity, belief momentum, switch probability, cue sensitivity and placement noise. The outcome of each model is the participant’s posterior mean, standardised within the analysed sample. Slopes are therefore in parameter SDs per questionnaire SD, which makes them comparable across parameters; the means and SDs of the standardisation are reported, so that every slope can be expressed in the units of the parameter.
STICSA state, STICSA trait, IU, BDI and OCI totals, each z-scored within the analysed sample. Each questionnaire enters its own model, as in RQ2; the questionnaires are not adjusted for each other.
Unordered factor with the two planned sum-to-zero contrasts
= (−1/2, 1/2, 0). With this coding the questionnaire term is the slope averaged over the three conditions, and its interactions with the two contrasts describe how the slope depends on the condition.

Three terms are tested for each parameter and questionnaire:
in the across-condition model (1 numerator df), and

(2 df) in the condition × questionnaire model. Each term is tested with an F-test against the model without it, which with the sum-to-zero coding is the Type III test. The slopes within each condition, in the two condition groups (C1 and C2 together, C3) and the two planned contrasts between conditions are estimated with

For each of the three terms, the Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied across the five questionnaires, separately for each parameter and sample (18 sets of five tests per sample). This mirrors the RQ2 models, in which the correction runs across the questionnaires within each model and term.
Distribution of the parameters and residuals.

The posterior means of cue sensitivity and placement noise are bimodal within C1 and C2 and concentrated near the upper prior bound in part of the sample (cue sensitivity in C3, where the instructions state the cue offset of 70°, which the model represents as a value of 1; placement noise for participants with the most variable placements, whose estimates reach the bound of 50°), and precision weighting, belief momentum and the switch probability are right-skewed.
(quartiles, skewness and the number of estimates and posterior intervals at each prior bound, by sample and condition), and

shows them. As a consequence, the residuals are not normal in most models. The three tested terms are therefore also tested with Wald F-tests based on a heteroscedasticity-consistent covariance matrix (HC3;
). The Shapiro-Wilk test of the residuals and the largest Cook’s distance are reported for every condition × questionnaire model.

The posterior mean treats each participant’s parameter as known. To carry the uncertainty of the estimates into the group-level analysis, both models are refitted on each of 100 posterior draws per participant, standardised with the mean and SD of the posterior means, and the coefficients are pooled with Rubin’s rules (
), with the degrees of freedom of

. This treats the posterior draws as plausible values. The fraction of missing information shows how much of the variance of a pooled coefficient is due to the uncertainty of the participants’ estimates.
Both models are fitted in two samples:
everyone with parameter estimates and questionnaire scores
participants for whom the latent-state model has the highest posterior probability in the model comparison
Which sample is primary is an open decision (front page, “Enforce the sequence model comparison → exclusion → parameter interpretation”). Both are reported until it is taken.
Differences from the earlier Python analysis

children.label: Differences from the earlier Python analysis

children.value: reported partial correlations, in which each questionnaire was adjusted for the other six scales, and regressions with a polynomial condition term. The present models enter one questionnaire at a time and use the planned contrasts of RQ2, so that RQ2 and RQ3 answer their questions in the same way. Associations found only after adjusting for the other scales (for example STICSA trait with the switch probability in run
) are therefore not expected to reappear here.
